body.statement:
For the finite inputs \(K,L,y,p^{1:L},N,\alpha\), the \(4K\) Clopper--Pearson intervals, and the generated component arrays \(A_\gamma,B_\gamma,b_\gamma,C_\gamma\), the finite common-rank inversion algorithm terminates.  If \(R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}\ne\varnothing\), it returns an exact finite-union extended formulation of \(C_n\), an exact common-parameter finite-union representation of every member of \(\mathcal H_n\), and the exact radii \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}\).  If \(R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}=\varnothing\), it returns the exact symbolic fallback \(C_n=[y_1,y_K]^L\), \(\mathcal H_n=\{A:\varnothing\ne A\subseteq[y_1,y_K]^L,\ A\text{ compact}\}\), \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}=y_K-y_1\), and \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}=(y_K-y_1)/2\); no finite-union polytope representation of each arbitrary fallback member is asserted.  In the unit-cost ordered-field model the nonempty branch uses at most
\[
(2m_{\mathrm{alg}}|\Gamma_K|)^{2^{O(v_{\mathrm{alg}})}}
\]
arithmetic and order operations, where \(|\Gamma_K|\le(2L+1)^2\binom{2K-2}{K-1}\); hence the procedure is finite for every fixed input.
body.justification: The theorem turns the nonconvex path representation into a terminating exact procedure for both reported confidence objects and their metric informativeness.
body.gap: Finite categorical instrumental-variable programs handle one convex compatibility region; they do not compute Hausdorff radii for a common-parameter collection of law-dependent nonconvex path unions.
body.consumer: Oregon Medicaid analysts can compute exact outer regions and diagnose their Hausdorff width before reporting extrapolations at support boundaries.
body.proof_tex:
There are at most \(2L+1\) weak positions of either propensity relative to the fixed grid (one of the \(L+1\) open intervals or a tie with one of at most \(L\) distinct grid values).  Hence
\[
|\Omega(p^{1:L})|\le(2L+1)^2,\qquad
|\Gamma_K|\le(2L+1)^2\binom{2K-2}{K-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
All these sets are finite and can be enumerated.  Suppose first that \(R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}\ne\varnothing\).

For a fixed \(\gamma\), the defining restrictions of \(R_n\), \(\overline{\mathcal Q}\), \(\overline\omega\), and \(A_\gamma x=b_\gamma+B_\gamma q'\), \(x\ge0\), are finitely many affine equalities and inequalities.  Thus \(\mathcal P_\gamma\) is a polytope.  The path-representation theorem gives, without relaxation,
\[
C_n=\bigcup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_K}
\{C_\gamma x:(q',x)\in\mathcal P_\gamma\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Keeping the same law variable \(q'\) across all feasible component images gives the exact common-parameter representation
\[
\mathcal H_n
=\left\{
\bigcup_{\gamma:q'\in D_\gamma}\{C_\gamma x:A_\gamma x=b_\gamma+B_\gamma q',\ x\ge0\}:
q'\in R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}
\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
This common variable is essential: allowing a different \(q'\) for each path would enlarge the collection.

For compact sets represented by (2)--(3), the assertion \(d_H(A,B)\le r\) is the conjunction of the two directed statements
\[
\forall a\in A\ \exists b\in B:\ \|a-b\|_\infty\le r,
\qquad
\forall b\in B\ \exists a\in A:\ \|a-b\|_\infty\le r.
\tag{4}
\]
Membership in each finite union is a finite disjunction, and \(\|a-b\|_\infty\le r\) is a finite list of affine inequalities.  Therefore (4), the supremum defining \(r_n^{\mathrm{out}}\), and the infimum--supremum defining \(r_n^{\mathrm{set}}\) are formulas in linear real arithmetic with at most \(v_{\mathrm{alg}}\) quantified real variables and at most \(2m_{\mathrm{alg}}|\Gamma_K|\) affine atoms after the two directed clauses are expanded.

Eliminate one quantified variable by collecting its affine lower and upper bounds and imposing every lower--upper comparison; negation converts universal to existential elimination.  If a formula has \(m\) atoms before a step, this produces at most \(m^2\) atoms.  Repeating for at most \(v\) variables gives at most
\[
m^{2^{O(v)}}
\]
arithmetic and order operations, including Boolean distribution among the finitely many component disjunctions.  Applying this with \(m=2m_{\mathrm{alg}}|\Gamma_K|\) proves the displayed unit-cost bound.  The resulting quantifier-free formula in \(r\) is a finite union of intervals and points; comparison of its finitely many affine boundary values isolates exactly the relevant infimum or supremum, whether or not it is attained.  Thus the algorithm terminates and returns the exact two radii.

If \(R_n\cap\overline{\mathcal Q}=\varnothing\), the algorithm tests this finite affine system and invokes the stipulated deterministic branch.  It then outputs \([y_1,y_K]^L\), the prescribed collection of all nonempty compact subsets, \(y_K-y_1\), and \((y_K-y_1)/2\).  The last radius is exact because the midpoint singleton is within \((y_K-y_1)/2\) of every nonempty compact subset in sup-norm Hausdorff distance, while the two opposite-corner singletons force a radius at least half their distance.  This verifies every output, including the fallback.
